title: McGill Entrance Scholarship Program
program_type: University merit-based entrance scholarship awarded at admission; one-year scholarships are automatic on the admission application while renewable Major Entrance Scholarships require a separate application submitted on the Undergraduate Admissions Applicant Portal
funding_type: Merit-based partial tuition scholarship (university-funded) worth CAD $3,000 for one year, or CAD $12,000-$48,000 in total ($3,000-$12,000 per annum, renewable up to four years) for Major Entrance Scholarships; a need-based Entrance Bursary Program is administered separately
administering_authority: McGill University - Scholarships and Student Aid Office, Brown Student Services Building, 3600 McTavish Street, Suite 3200, Montreal, Quebec H3A 0G3, Canada
implementing_agency: McGill University - Scholarships and Student Aid Office (identical to the administering authority; major scholarship finalists are determined by selection committees and awards fall under the jurisdiction of the Committee on Enrolment and Student Affairs, CESA)
programme_action: McGill centrally-administered Entrance Scholarship Program - two award types: One-year Entrance Scholarships (CAD $3,000, non-renewable) and Major Entrance Scholarships (CAD $12,000-$48,000 total; CAD $3,000, $5,000, $10,000 or $12,000 per annum, renewable up to three or four years)
description: McGill University's centrally-administered Entrance Scholarship Program is a merit-based funding scheme for first-time university students entering a full-time undergraduate degree program, and it is open to applicants of any citizenship, including international applicants from schools outside Canada and the United States. All applicants are automatically considered for a one-year entrance scholarship worth CAD $3,000 if they meet the estimated minimum academic requirements, with no separate application required, while renewable Major Entrance Scholarships require a separate application from October 1 with two letters of reference. McGill's Scholarships and Student Aid Office reports that in its last admission cycle it offered over CAD $6.2 million in one-year and renewable entrance scholarships to more than 2,000 students, including US and international students. International applicants should read this programme together with McGill's separate need-based Entrance Bursary Program, for which McGill states that financial need is considered for all students including international students.

award_types: One-year entrance scholarships (CAD $3,000, non-renewable) - automatic consideration, no separate application
Major Entrance Scholarships (CAD $12,000-$48,000 total; CAD $3,000, $5,000, $10,000 or $12,000 per annum, renewable up to three or four years) - separate application required
McGill Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong Entrance Scholarship (one-year, CAD $10,000) - separate application, restricted to Chinese citizens or Hong Kong permanent residents

One-Year Community Leadership Entrance Award (CAD $5,000) - separate application, rewards Quebec students for leadership in social justice, racial justice, inclusion and community-building initiatives
Faculty-specific entrance scholarships administered by the Schulich School of Music, Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences, Law and Medicine - not transferable if the recipient changes faculty
programme_structure.award_types_detail: There are two types of centrally-administered entrance scholarships. One-year scholarships are valued at CAD $3,000 and are non-renewable. Major entrance scholarships are valued between CAD $12,000 and CAD $48,000, equivalent to CAD $3,000 to CAD $12,000 per annum renewable for up to four years provided the criteria for renewal are met. CAD $12,000 scholarships are only available to Canadian citizens or legal permanent residents of Canada. Recipients of McGill centrally-administered entrance scholarships can receive only one scholarship; where more than one offer is made, the final award is the highest eligible value, which does not affect faculty-specific entrance scholarships.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Renewable entrance scholarships are tenable until completion of a first undergraduate degree, to a maximum of three or four years, provided the renewal criteria are met. Recipients must complete 27 McGill graded credits during the regular academic year (Fall and Winter terms), or 14 McGill graded credits if registered for only one term; summer courses are not counted and credits transferred due to advanced standing (AP, IB, French Baccalaureate, A-Levels) are excluded. A probationary sessional GPA of 3.50 on a minimum of 27 McGill graded credits is required in the first year of study, and a minimum sessional GPA of 3.70 on at least 27 graded credits in the second year and all subsequent years. Pre-Med and Pre-Dent CEGEP students must meet the same first-year requirement and thereafter achieve Dean's Honour List standing (top 10%) in Medicine or Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences; Law students must place in the top 10 per cent of the faculty cohort or Dean's Honour List. Non-renewal can be appealed to the Scholarships Review Subcommittee with documented extenuating circumstances.
programme_structure.application_required: Partly. One-year entrance scholarships require no separate application - all first-time university students entering a full-time undergraduate degree program are automatically considered. Major Entrance Scholarships require a separate application submitted on the Undergraduate Admissions Applicant Portal soon after submitting the application for admission; the application opens October 1. Students who apply for but do not receive a major scholarship are automatically considered for a one-year entrance scholarship with no additional application.
programme_structure.intake: September (Fall) entry, with applications opening October 1 of the preceding year. McGill also operates a January (Winter semester) admission route for selected programs.
ineligible_applicants: Diploma of Collegial Studies (DEC) entrants outside the centralised scheme
From Fall 2026, CEGEP students admitted to BCL/JD (Law), Dent-P (Dentistry) or Med-P (Medicine)

verification_type: Direct verification from official mcgill.ca admission and student aid pages, the official Student Awards calendar, the McGill course catalogue regulations PDF, and an authenticated asset check of the McGill University logo on the mcgill.ca domain.
verification_notes: All amounts, award names, deadlines, academic minima and English proficiency minimums in this record were taken directly from official mcgill.ca pages read on 2026-10-10. McGill publishes no monthly stipend, travel allowance, installation allowance or insurance component for entrance scholarships, and publishes no individual per-award value for most donor-named awards, so those fields are null rather than estimated. McGill also publishes no per-cycle award count for international recipients specifically and no universal selection weighting. The international tuition rate itself is published only in PDF fee tables that could not be extracted as machine-readable text, so no international tuition dollar figure is recorded here; the existence of the Guaranteed Tuition Model for international students in bachelor's degrees is recorded as verified. No official mcgill.ca page was found that uses the term 'need-blind' for international undergraduate admission, so that claim is deliberately not asserted.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Applications open October 1. Major Entrance Scholarship deadlines by applicant region: January 21 for applicants from schools outside of Canada, February 7 for applicants from schools in Ontario and the rest of Canada, and March 7 for applicants from Quebec CEGEPs. The corresponding admission application deadlines are January 15, February 1 and March 1 respectively, with supporting documents due March 1 for schools outside Canada.
application_deadline.application_period: October 1, 2026 (opening of the admission application and the Major Entrance Scholarship application) to January 21, 2027 at midnight, Montreal time, for September 2027 entry
application_deadline.official_rule: McGill's Applying for Entrance Scholarships page states: 'Do not wait to be admitted to McGill to apply for a scholarship. Apply by the following deadlines: applicants from a Quebec CEGEP - March 7; applicants from a school in the rest of Canada - February 7; applicants from a school outside of Canada - January 21.' The same page adds that 'All major entrance scholarship applications must be submitted online via the Undergraduate Admissions Applicant Portal, no later than midnight, Montreal time (Eastern Standard Time), on the deadline dates listed above.' The admission deadline table for other international high schools lists Application for admission January 15, Supporting documents March 1, Major Entrance Scholarship application and documents January 21, and McGill Financial Aid application 30 days from acceptance date.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The Major Entrance Scholarship deadline does not move even if an applicant is granted permission to submit a late admission application, and McGill states that late applications will not be considered for scholarships. All supporting documents (two letters of reference and the signed school rank statement) must also be submitted by January 21 for applicants from schools outside Canada.

programme_duration.official_range: One-year entrance scholarships are tenable only for the first two semesters of the undergraduate program, excluding the summer semester. Renewable entrance scholarships are tenable until completion of a first undergraduate degree, to a maximum of three or four years.
programme_duration.renewal_note: McGill expresses award tenability in academic years rather than a single duration figure, so the year and month fields are null. Renewal requires 27 McGill graded credits per regular academic year (14 if registered for a single term), a probationary sessional GPA of 3.50 in the first year and a sessional GPA of 3.70 thereafter, and excludes advanced-standing transfer credits. First-time entrance scholarships cannot be deferred unless deferred admission is granted, in which case the highest-value offer is deferred for up to one year and no new major scholarship application is entertained in the second year.

funding.scholarship_type: Merit-based entrance scholarship. Separately, McGill administers a need-based Entrance Bursary Program (non-repayable awards) for students from low- to modest-income families.
funding.monthly_amount_note: McGill publishes no monthly stipend for entrance scholarships. Scholarships and monetary awards are credited to the student fee account, one-half for each of the Fall and Winter terms.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel, airfare or relocation allowance is published for McGill entrance scholarships.
funding.fully_funded_note: McGill entrance scholarships are partial awards. No centrally-administered McGill entrance scholarship covers full tuition plus living costs for international students: the top renewable Major Entrance Scholarship package is CAD $48,000 over up to four years, and the CAD $12,000-per-annum tier is restricted to Canadian citizens and legal permanent residents. Non-monetary benefits are residence priority and priority registration. International students are additionally charged a mandatory international health insurance fee and a CAD $1,000 confirmation-of-acceptance deposit, both of which are costs borne by the student.

tuition.amount: CAD $3,000 one-off, or CAD $12,000-$48,000 in total (CAD $3,000, $5,000, $10,000 or $12,000 per annum, renewable up to three or four years)
tuition.conditions: Credited to the student fee account, one-half for each of the Fall and Winter terms. To receive full payment the recipient must be registered full time (minimum 12 McGill graded credits per term and 27 per academic year) in an undergraduate degree program; a recipient registered for only one term must complete 14 McGill graded credits to receive 50 per cent of the value. If the award exceeds fees, a refund can be requested from Student Accounts after September 30 and after January 30.

visa_support.note: Not published in official source. Immigration support is provided separately by McGill's International Student Services and is not a scholarship benefit.

insurance.note: Not published in official source. International students are charged a mandatory international health insurance fee rather than being covered by the award.

accommodation_support.conditions: Non-monetary. All entrance scholarship awardees entering university in September are guaranteed one of their top three choices of residence building, provided they apply by the residence application deadline; where a smaller residence building fills, the second or third choice is guaranteed. All September entrants are also eligible for priority registration for their first year of study. No accommodation grant is published.

bond.note: No service bond, return-of-service obligation or employment condition attaches to a McGill entrance scholarship. Renewal depends only on credit load and GPA standing, and there is no residency or nationality bond.

total_estimated_value.note: McGill publishes no combined total value for the programme. The maximum published renewable Major Entrance Scholarship package is CAD $48,000 over up to four years; the one-year award is CAD $3,000.

coverage: Partial tuition and compulsory fees, credited one-half to each of the Fall and Winter terms
CAD $3,000 for one year (one-year entrance scholarship, non-renewable)
CAD $12,000-$48,000 in total for renewable Major Entrance Scholarships (CAD $3,000-$12,000 per annum)
Guaranteed one of the top three residence building choices for September entrants who apply by the residence application deadline
Priority course registration for the first year of study
Prestige Scholars Mentorship Program for recipients of Prestige (CAD $10,000), Greville Smith (CAD $12,000) and Schulich Leaders Engineering or Science scholarships
coverage_limitations: Entrance scholarships are partial awards and do not cover full tuition, living costs, flights, books or health insurance; there is no monthly stipend.
One-year entrance scholarships are worth CAD $3,000 and are not renewable.
CAD $12,000 Major Entrance Scholarships are only available to Canadian citizens or legal permanent residents of Canada and are therefore not available to international applicants.

McGill reserves the right to change information in the Undergraduate Scholarships and Awards Calendar, including correcting errors, altering award values and revising or cancelling particular awards, without prior notification.
The exact benefit structure may differ for individual donor-named awards listed in the calendar, most of which are published as 'Award value: Varies'.
Faculty-specific entrance scholarships in Music, Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences, Law and Medicine are administered separately and are not transferable if the recipient changes faculty.
No per-award dollar value, total value or universal selection weighting is published, so no total value is asserted in this record.
eligible_applicants: First-time university students entering a full-time undergraduate degree program at McGill, of any citizenship, including international applicants from schools outside Canada and the United States

Applicants who hold a recognised academic pre-university diploma leading to university studies in their country of study (A-Levels, International Baccalaureate, French Baccalaureate, national high school diplomas and other credentials listed by McGill)
Final-year secondary school applicants, since interim, mid-year or predicted results are reviewed
Applicants from schools in the rest of Canada and Quebec CEGEPs, who follow the same programme under different regional deadlines
final_year_condition: Final-year secondary school applicants are eligible. Applicants must have obtained, prior to the start of classes, a recognised academic pre-university diploma leading to university studies in their country of study. McGill reviews interim, mid-year or first-semester results of the final year and accepts predicted A-Level, IB and French Baccalaureate results. Studies in applied programs, or at vocational or technical high schools, are not normally considered for admission consideration.
equivalent_degree_note: McGill evaluates applicants on the normal basis for admission in their country of study and publishes an accepted-international-credentials list by country, including Abitur (Germany), Matura (Austria, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia), Apolytirion (Greece), Senior Secondary Certificate of Education (Australia), Senior High School Graduation Diploma (China PRC), Senior School Certificate (India, Nigeria), Senior Secondary School Certificate (Bangladesh), Hong Kong Advanced Levels and the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education, Singapore-Cambridge GCE Advanced Level, National Certificate of Educational Achievement (New Zealand), Ylioppilastukintotodistus (Finland), Studentereksamen (Denmark) and Slutbetyg fran Gymnasieskola (Sweden). McGill states it welcomes qualified applicants from Bologna-signatory countries and that qualified applicants to Arts, Education and Management with a Bologna-compliant diploma leading to a three-year European undergraduate program will be admissible to a three-year McGill program, with Management students required to complete additional mathematics coursework.
previous_award_restriction: Recipients of McGill centrally-administered entrance scholarships can receive only one scholarship. Where more than one offer is received, the final entrance scholarship is that of the highest eligible value; this does not affect faculty-specific entrance scholarships. There is no Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters restriction because this is a bachelor's-level award.

eligibility.citizenship: No citizenship restriction applies to the centrally-administered Entrance Scholarship Program. McGill states that all students who apply are considered for merit-based entrance scholarships regardless of citizenship, and that all new first-year students are eligible to apply for funding regardless of citizenship. Two named sub-awards are nationality-specific: the McGill Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong Entrance Scholarship (one-year CAD $10,000) is restricted to Chinese citizens or Hong Kong permanent residents holding a valid Hong Kong S.A.R. identity document, applying from the Chinese Mainland or Hong Kong S.A.R., and applicants holding Canadian permanent residence are not eligible; the One-Year Community Leadership Entrance Award (CAD $5,000) rewards Quebec students.
eligibility.residence_requirement: None for scholarship eligibility. Applicants must be entering a full-time undergraduate degree program at McGill. Applicants who hold Canadian permanent residence are ineligible only for the McGill Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong Entrance Scholarship.
eligibility.age_limit: No age limit is published for entrance scholarships. No age cap or minimum is stated on any official page read.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Completion of a recognised academic pre-university diploma leading to university studies in the applicant's country of study, obtained prior to the start of classes. Applicants are reviewed on their high school transcript with particular emphasis on yearly averages and results in prerequisite subjects, and prerequisites must have been completed during the last two years of high school. Applied, vocational and technical high school programs are not normally considered.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Estimated scholarship minima by admit type: Quebec CEGEP, a minimum 36 overall cote de rendement au collegial (CRC); Canadian high school outside Quebec and Ontario, a minimum 97 per cent average on all academic grade 12 and grade 11 level courses and/or rank in the top 1 per cent of class; Ontario high school, a minimum 97 per cent overall average on all 3U, 3M, 4U and 4M courses and/or rank in the top 1 per cent of class; overseas high school, a minimum A average (approximately 97.0 per cent or equivalent) over the last two years of full-time study and/or rank in the top 1 per cent of class; Advanced Levels, a minimum of four A-Level/CAPE/Pre-U subjects with predicted or final grades of A*A*A*A (or AAAA where the exam board does not award A*, such as Caribbean CAPE, Scottish Advanced/Highers and Singapore A-Levels), plus AS and GCSE/IGCSE/O-Level results also with A grades; International Baccalaureate, 41 subject points not including bonus points on predicted or final grades; French Baccalaureate, a minimum overall average of 18 with a minimum score of 15 in each course; United States high school, a minimum A, 4.00 GPA or equivalent unweighted average over the last two years of full-time studies plus a minimum SAT score of 730 in each section or a minimum ACT composite score of 33.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: For overseas high school applicants, the estimated minimum is an A average, approximately 97.0 per cent or equivalent, over the last two years of full-time study, and/or rank in the top 1 per cent of class. McGill labels the entire table as estimated minima based on averages from historical data, states that the minima are for consideration only and may be lower or higher depending on available scholarship funds and the number of applicants, and states that the table is for reference purposes only. Meeting the standard does not guarantee a scholarship.
eligibility.language_requirement: Proof of English proficiency is required unless an exemption applies. Acceptable minimums are IELTS Academic overall band 6.5 with individual component scores of 6.0; TOEFL 90 on the 120-point scale (or 4.5 on the six-point scale for tests taken as of January 21, 2026) with component minima of Reading 21, Listening 21, Writing 21 and Speaking 21 (or 4.5, 4.5, 4.5 and 4.0 on the six-point scale); Duolingo English Test 125 (130 for B.Ed. TESL and B.Com.); PTE Academic overall 65 with individual component scores of 60; CAEL overall band 70 with individual component scores of 60; Cambridge C2 Proficiency with a Grade C or better; Cambridge C1 Advanced with a Grade B or better; or a McGill Certificate of Proficiency in English (Language and Culture, English for Professional Communication, or Bilingual Professional Communication). Education (TESL) and Management require a TOEFL score of 100 (5.0 on the six-point scale), and Music requires 79-80 (4.0). Programme-specific requirements must not be universalised.
eligibility.work_experience: Not required. No professional or work-experience requirement is published for entrance scholarships.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: For Major Entrance Scholarships, applicants must provide a factual list of their school activities and community/volunteer involvement for the last three academic years, including athletic, artistic and other activities, plus a general essay and a one-page third-person letter of reference written by the applicant about the applicant. One-year entrance scholarships are awarded solely on academic achievement and require no extracurricular record.
eligibility.financial_need: Financial need is not considered in the granting of entrance scholarships; McGill states they are entirely merit-based. Financial need is assessed separately under the need-based Entrance Bursary Program, for which McGill states that financial need is considered for all McGill students, including international students, and that international students who are not eligible for government aid may still apply for an Entrance Bursary based on demonstrated financial need.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Only one centrally-administered entrance scholarship may be held; the highest-value eligible offer stands. No restriction based on a previous scholarship from another institution is published.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Full-time undergraduate degree program. Transfer, Mature, Diploma, Exchange, Special, Part-time and Visiting students are not eligible for entrance scholarships. Beginning Fall 2026, CEGEP students admitted to BCL/JD (Law), Dent-P (Dentistry) or Med-P (Medicine) are no longer eligible for centralised McGill entrance scholarships; applicants to one of these programs and an eligible program may apply and be considered for the one-year scholarship, but become ineligible and must relinquish any offer if they accept Law, Medicine or Dentistry. Students registered with Student Accessibility and Achievement may be eligible for need-based aid while pursuing a reduced course load.
eligibility.health_requirement: No health requirement is published for scholarship eligibility. Mandatory immunisation requirements apply to admitted students in specific clinical programs such as Nursing and Social Work, and international students are charged a mandatory international health insurance fee.
eligibility.field_restrictions: All full-time undergraduate degree programs are eligible, subject to prerequisites. Professional programs are handled separately: faculty-specific entrance scholarships exist for Music, Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences, Law and Medicine, and applicants to Dentistry, Law or Medicine should inquire at the respective faculty admissions office. CEGEP entrants to Law, Dentistry and Medicine are excluded from the centralised scheme from Fall 2026.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: The published minima are explicitly estimated, not fixed. For overseas high school applicants the figure is a minimum A average, approximately 97.0 per cent or equivalent, over the last two years of full-time study, and/or rank in the top 1 per cent of class. McGill states that it is not possible to provide minimum criteria in advance, that the table provides estimated scholarship minima by admit type for the upcoming fall term based on averages from historical data, that the minima are for consideration only and may be lower or higher depending on available scholarship funds and the number of applicants, and that the table is for reference purposes only. McGill also states that applicants are not guaranteed a scholarship even if they meet the standards listed.
programme_specific_requirements: For international (overseas high school) applicants: a minimum A average, approximately 97.0 per cent or equivalent, over the last two years of full-time study, and/or rank in the top 1 per cent of class

International Baccalaureate: 41 subject points, not including bonus points, on predicted or final grades. For applicants at high schools in Canada or the United States completing a high school diploma concurrently with an IB Diploma, review for admission and scholarship is normally based on high school grades, with predicted IB results taken into additional consideration on a case-by-case basis

Advanced Levels: a minimum of four A-Level/CAPE/Pre-U subjects with predicted or final grades of A*A*A*A, plus AS (if written) and GCSE/IGCSE/O-Level results also with A grades; the minimum is AAAA on predicted or final results where the exam board does not award A* (Caribbean CAPE, Scottish Advanced/Highers, Singapore A-Levels)
French Baccalaureate: minimum overall average of 18, with a minimum score of 15 in each course
Quebec CEGEP: minimum 36 overall cote de rendement au collegial (CRC)
Canadian high school outside Quebec and Ontario, and Ontario high school: minimum 97 per cent average and/or rank in the top 1 per cent of class
Where class rank is available it should be provided; rank in the top 1 per cent is expected
selection_factors_may_include: Academic achievement, which is the first priority and the sole basis for one-year entrance scholarships
Outstanding leadership in school or community activities for Major Entrance Scholarships, where McGill states leadership constitutes more than simple participation in extracurricular activities
School activities and community/volunteer involvement over the last three academic years, including athletic, artistic and other activities
The general essay and the one-page third-person self-reference letter submitted as part of the Major Entrance Scholarship application
Two letters of reference (one academic and one activity-related)
Class rank and size, where the school provides such information
An interview for major scholarship finalists
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Major entrance scholarships are determined by selection committees and awarded on the basis of academic achievement and outstanding leadership, with emphasis placed on academic excellence as the first priority followed by demonstrated leadership. Applications are reviewed by members of the selection committees that determine the finalists, and finalists may be interviewed. There is no reconsideration of additional or final results, and scholarship decisions are made during the admission process based on the academic information available at that time.

english_requirement.moi_rule: An applicant does not need to provide proof of English proficiency if any of the following applies: they have lived and attended high school and/or university for at least four consecutive years in a country where English is the acknowledged primary language (McGill's list includes Australia, Canada including Quebec, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, the United States, Singapore, South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, Jamaica, Malta and others); they have completed a DEC at a French CEGEP in Quebec together with the Quebec Secondary V diploma; they have completed a DEC at an English CEGEP in Quebec; they have completed or will complete the International French Baccalaureate (BFI) American or British section, or the previous Option Internationale (OIB); they have completed or will complete an International Baccalaureate Group 1 English subject (Language A: Literature, Language A: Language and Literature, or Literature and Performance) with a 5 or better; they have completed or will complete English as Language 1 or Language 2 in the European Baccalaureate curriculum in the Schola Europaea system; they have completed or will complete British Curriculum A-Level English with a final grade of C or better; or they have completed the British Curriculum GCSE/IGCSE/GCE O-Level English, English Language, English First Language or English as a Second Language with a final grade of B (or 5) or better.
english_requirement.test_score_note: The language of instruction at McGill University is English and all applicants, unless exempt, must demonstrate the required level of English proficiency regardless of citizenship status or country of origin. The Admissions Office reserves the right to request proof of English proficiency from any applicant, regardless of citizenship, country of origin or first language, at any time during the review process. Results must come directly from the examining institution to McGill; applicants are not able to upload results, and McGill's strong preference is to receive results electronically directly from the issuing organisation. Institutional versions of the tests are not accepted. The IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted, and McGill accepts only scores submitted electronically by IELTS, not paper Test Report Forms. McGill does not use TOEFL MyBest scores. TOEFL score minima are published on two scales: 90 on the 120-point scale for tests up to January 20, 2026, and 4.5 on the six-point scale for tests as of January 21, 2026; McGill advises that score minima can change at any time. Programme-specific higher minimums apply to Education (TESL) and Management, which require TOEFL 100 (5.0 on the six-point scale) and Duolingo 130, and a lower programme-specific minimum applies to Music at TOEFL 79-80 (4.0). The TOEFL institutional code at McGill University is 0935-00. Component minima are IELTS 6.0 in each component; TOEFL Reading 21, Listening 21, Writing 21, Speaking 21 (4.5, 4.5, 4.5 and 4.0 on the six-point scale); PTE Academic 60 in each component; CAEL 60 in each component.
accepted_tests: IELTS Academic (overall band 6.5, components 6.0) - One Skill Retake not accepted, electronic submission only
TOEFL iBT (90 on the 120-point scale, or 4.5 on the six-point scale; institutional code 0935-00)
Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic) (overall 65, components 60)
Duolingo English Test (DET) (125; 130 for B.Ed. TESL and B.Com.)
Canadian Academic English Language Assessment (CAEL) (overall band 70, components 60) - paper, computer and online editions accepted
Cambridge C2 Proficiency, formerly Certificate of Proficiency in English (Grade C or better)
Cambridge C1 Advanced, formerly Certificate in Advanced English (Grade B or better)
McGill Certificate of Proficiency - English Language and Culture, English for Professional Communication, or Bilingual Professional Communication

language_of_instruction.language_note: The language of instruction at McGill University is English. McGill states that French proficiency is not a general admission requirement and that students will not need to demonstrate proficiency in French to graduate; participation in French-language learning opportunities is entirely optional. However, a number of programs - including Medicine, Nursing, Dentistry, Dietetics and Law - already require, or take into consideration, proficiency in French, and French proficiency remains an admission requirement for selected undergraduate programs, so program-specific requirements should be verified with the relevant admissions advisors.

application_method.application_route: Two-step online route. First submit the application for admission on the McGill Applicant Portal at future.mcgill.ca/apply from October 1 and pay the CAD $140.16 non-refundable application fee; one-year entrance scholarships then require no further action because consideration is automatic. Second, for renewable Major Entrance Scholarships, complete the separate entrance scholarship application, which unlocks on the same Undergraduate Admissions Applicant Portal from October 1 once the admission application has been submitted and acknowledged, and submit it by January 21 (midnight Montreal time) for applicants from schools outside Canada, together with two letters of reference submitted directly by the referees and the signed school rank statement. Applicants are explicitly told not to wait to be admitted to McGill before applying for a scholarship.
application_steps: Step 1 - Decide what to study using McGill's program finder, which lists over 300 undergraduate programs.

Step 2 - Make sure you are eligible by selecting your educational background and reviewing admission requirements, prerequisites, previous years' admission scores and the deadline dates that apply to you.

Step 3 - Submit your application online on the McGill Applicant Portal from October 1 and pay the CAD $140.16 non-refundable application fee. A second application to another program in the same term and level is free; each further application costs CAD $140.16.

Step 4 - Apply for an entrance scholarship. One-year entrance scholarships are automatic. For Major Entrance Scholarships, complete the separate online application on the Undergraduate Admissions Applicant Portal, providing the three-year activity list, the general essay and the one-page third-person self-reference letter, and arrange for two referees to submit letters directly.

Step 5 - Submit documents and keep in touch: upload all grades and interim grades granted up to the admissions application deadline, forward subsequent interim or final grades to the admissions office as soon as they are issued, upload the high school transcript, and arrange for official English test results to be sent directly to McGill. Monitor the McGill Applicant Portal and email regularly.
application_method.application_fee: CAD $140.16 (non-refundable). selection_process.decision_maker: McGill's Scholarships and Student Aid Office, with major scholarship finalists determined by selection committees. Scholarships and awards fall under the jurisdiction of the Committee on Enrolment and Student Affairs (CESA), and the central University program of awards is administered by the Scholarships and Student Aid Office.
selection_process.selection_type: Merit-based. One-year entrance scholarships are awarded solely on academic achievement and require no application. Major Entrance Scholarships are determined by selection committees on academic achievement and outstanding leadership.
possible_stages: Submission of the application for admission and, where relevant, the separate Major Entrance Scholarship application with supporting documents

Renewal review at the end of each academic year after final marks are entered, with notification of renewal or non-renewal by Scholarships and Student Aid
selection_process.weighting_note: McGill publishes no numerical weighting. It states only that emphasis is placed on academic excellence as the first priority, followed by demonstrated leadership, and that leadership constitutes more than simple participation in extracurricular activities. One-year scholarships are awarded solely on academic achievement. No percentage weighting is published for any criterion, so no universal weighting is recorded.
selection_process.results_timing: Named entrance scholarship decisions are communicated to recipients in late July and August, with payment effected in the upcoming academic year. Admission decisions for applicants from high schools outside the United States and Canada are released from mid-November to mid-May for September entry, with offers generally issued to the most competitive applicants first and all dates subject to change without prior notice. Scholarship offers are communicated only to applicants who receive them, by email to the address on the admission application.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: There is no published ranking of applicants or of award tiers. Where a student receives more than one offer of a centrally-administered entrance scholarship, the final award is the highest eligible value. Students who apply for but do not receive a major scholarship are automatically reconsidered for a one-year entrance scholarship with no additional application, and there is no reconsideration of additional or final results once a scholarship decision has been made.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree in the chosen McGill undergraduate program, for example Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Science, Bachelor of Commerce, Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Education, Bachelor of Fine Arts, Bachelor of Music, Bachelor of Nursing, Bachelor of Social Work or Bachelor of Arts and Science
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Three to four years depending on faculty and entering credential. McGill admits qualified applicants to Arts, Education and Management holding a Bologna-compliant diploma that leads to a three-year European undergraduate program to a three-year McGill program; Management students must complete additional mathematics coursework. The minimum residency requirement is 60 credits completed at McGill to qualify for a McGill undergraduate degree.
possible_awards: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Environmental Sciences (BSc(AgEnvSc))
degree_outcome.degree_note: Entrance scholarships are tenable only toward a first undergraduate degree. Renewable entrance scholarships are tenable until completion of a first undergraduate degree, to a maximum of three or four years, provided the renewal criteria are met. Certain professional degrees - Dentistry (DMD), Medicine and MDCM (MDCM), and Law (BCL/JD) - run on their own schedules and their faculties administer separate entrance scholarships; from Fall 2026, CEGEP entrants to Law, Dentistry and Medicine are excluded from the centralised programme.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Credits transferred to McGill due to advanced standing (AP, IB, French Baccalaureate, A-Levels and similar) are excluded from the 27 McGill graded credits required to hold and retain a McGill entrance scholarship. Courses taken at other Quebec universities through the Inter-University Transfer (IUT) Agreement may be counted toward scholarship renewal requirements or consideration for other academic awards, to a maximum of 3 credits per semester or 6 credits per annum, with eligibility based on all courses taken during the regular academic year and the combined McGill GPA plus the global GPA including IUT credits. Recipients of renewable entrance scholarships may retain their award while registered full time at another university for up to one year on a faculty-approved program forming part of the McGill degree requirements, but must submit host transcripts for equivalency determination.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Recipients continue to pay the applicable tuition rate for their residency status. For undergraduate students admitted as of Fall 2026, McGill operates a Guaranteed Tuition Model for international students in a bachelor's, DMD or MDCM degree, under which the international tuition rate is set and held for the duration of the student's time at McGill, eliminating year-over-year increases. For comparison, published 2026-27 rates are CAD $103.92 per credit at the Quebec rate and CAD $432.85 per credit (Rate A) for Canadian students admitted since Fall 2024; the international rate is published only in PDF fee tables that could not be extracted as machine-readable text, so no international dollar rate is asserted here.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No application-fee waiver for entrance scholarship recipients is published. The application fee is CAD $140.16, non-refundable, with a free second application to another program in the same term and level.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Newly admitted entrance scholarship recipients should note that their offers are conditional upon being accepted for admission. McGill states that it is the responsibility of every undergraduate student to apprise themselves of the regulations, conditions and criteria governing their scholarships and awards, and recipients must acquaint themselves with all regulations pertaining to both one-year and major entrance scholarships.
common_services: McGill Work Study Program - on-campus job opportunities for full-time degree students in financial need; students receiving need-based aid are automatically approved to apply upon application via Minerva

Tuition payment deferrals - deferral of tuition fee payment without interest or penalty, available to government aid recipients and international students experiencing delays in transferring funds, initiated by a Fee Deferral application in Minerva
In-Course Financial Aid Program - bursaries, short- and long-term loans and Work Study for full-time undergraduate degree students in subsequent years
Frugal Scholar Money Management Program - financial planning, debt management and educational cost workshops, plus a Financial Roadmap for Undergraduates
International Student Services - immigration documents, health insurance, work permits and pre-arrival orientation webinars

Student Accessibility and Achievement - accommodations, including an exception to the graded-credits requirement for renewal with documentation, and eligibility for need-based aid on a reduced course load
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: None. No service bond, return-of-service obligation, residency requirement, nationality condition or employment commitment attaches to a McGill entrance scholarship.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: Not applicable, because there is no bond. The consequences that do apply are academic and administrative: the award or part of it is cancelled if the recipient is not registered full time, and renewal is not considered if the 27 graded credits or the applicable GPA standing are not met. Non-renewal for reasons such as illness can be appealed to the Scholarships Review Subcommittee with a written explanation, supporting documentation and a signed consent form. McGill reserves the right to revoke admission, scholarship and financial support in cases of misrepresentation, and students on internship have awards deferred while those who do not register for a term or year are deemed to have relinquished the award.

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: McGill does not request a conventional motivation letter for admission, but the Major Entrance Scholarship application requires three written components that function as one. Use the factual activity list to show sustained, deepening commitment over three academic years rather than a long list of one-off memberships, since McGill explicitly defines leadership as more than simple participation. Use the general essay to show how a specific person or experience changed the applicant's outlook, with concrete detail and reflection rather than general admiration. Use the one-page third-person self-reference letter as a candid, evidence-backed self-assessment that corroborates the referees' accounts instead of repeating the activity list. Frame academic results as the primary evidence, since academic excellence is McGill's stated first priority, and connect leadership and service to a coherent trajectory.

risk_flags.risk: Deadline misreading between the January 21 scholarship deadline and the January 15 admission deadline
risk_flags.impact: An applicant who tracks only the admission deadline will miss the Major Entrance Scholarship application and lose eligibility for any renewable award worth up to CAD $48,000.
risk_flags.mitigation: Record both dates separately with the exact source wording, note that the scholarship deadline does not move even when late admission is permitted, and submit the scholarship application as soon as it unlocks on October 1 rather than waiting for an admission decision.

risk_flags.risk: Citizenship restriction on the top renewable tier
risk_flags.impact: International applicants cannot receive the CAD $12,000-per-annum major scholarship, which is restricted to Canadian citizens and legal permanent residents, so the realistic maximum for an international recipient is lower than the advertised CAD $48,000 range.
risk_flags.mitigation: State the restriction explicitly in coverage_limitations and in the eligibility block, and avoid presenting CAD $48,000 as an achievable international value.

risk_flags.risk: Estimated rather than guaranteed academic minima
risk_flags.impact: A student who meets the published A or 97 per cent average may still receive no scholarship, because McGill states the table is for reference only, that minima may be lower or higher depending on funds and applicant volume, and that meeting the standards guarantees nothing.
risk_flags.mitigation: Label all minima as estimated in academic_requirements and in the percentage_note, and pair them with the statement that there is no reconsideration of additional or final results.

risk_flags.risk: Conflation of merit scholarships with need-based aid
risk_flags.impact: Presenting entrance scholarships as need-sensitive, or presenting the Entrance Bursary Program as a scholarship, misrepresents both. McGill states entrance scholarships are entirely merit-based and financial need is not considered, while the bursary is a separate non-repayable need-based award.
risk_flags.mitigation: Keep the two programmes in separate fields, set selection_criteria.financial_need to false for the scholarship, and record the bursary in programme_structure, funding and database_notes as a distinct programme.

risk_flags.risk: Contradictory statements about international need-based eligibility
risk_flags.impact: The entrance bursary page states financial need is considered for all students including international students, while the in-course need page states first-year international students are generally not eligible for need-based aid from McGill. A reader could over-promise need-based funding to international applicants.
risk_flags.mitigation: Quote both statements in database_notes with their URLs, record the entrance bursary as the pathway for first-year international applicants, and flag the in-course restriction as a limitation on aid in later years.

risk_flags.risk: Unverified claim that McGill is need-blind for international admission
risk_flags.impact: No official mcgill.ca page read for this record uses the term 'need-blind' for international undergraduate admission, so asserting it would be an unverifiable claim that could mislead applicants about admission and aid.
risk_flags.mitigation: Do not assert need-blind status anywhere in the record. Instead record the verified facts: scholarships are merit-based, need is not considered for scholarships, admission is based on academic merit and space availability, and need-based aid is assessed separately. Record the absence of an official need-blind statement in verification.unverified_or_removed_claims.

risk_flags.risk: Award values and individual donor awards can change or be cancelled without notice
risk_flags.impact: The Undergraduate Scholarships and Awards Calendar disclaimer reserves the right to correct errors, alter award values and revise or cancel particular awards without prior notification, and most donor-named awards publish 'Award value: Varies'.
risk_flags.mitigation: Cite the disclaimer in coverage_limitations, avoid totalling awards into a single value, and set total_estimated_value to unavailable with the reason stated.

risk_flags.risk: Partial funding leaves a large residual cost for international students
risk_flags.impact: Even a maximum renewable award leaves most international tuition, the CAD $1,000 confirmation deposit and the mandatory international health insurance fee to be met by the student, and McGill states most international students are not eligible for government assistance and are responsible for securing funding.
risk_flags.mitigation: Set fully_funded to false with an explicit note, list the residual costs, and point to tuition payment deferrals, Work Study and emergency loans as the available stopgaps.

database_notes: Scope and naming. This record covers McGill University's centrally-administered Entrance Scholarship Program as the umbrella for international undergraduate scholarships, together with the surrounding international student funding structure that applicants must consider alongside it. The official name used for the award title is 'McGill Entrance Scholarship Program'; McGill also refers to the same scheme as 'Entrance Scholarships', 'centrally-administered entrance scholarships', 'McGill's Entrance Scholarship Program' and 'McGill's Entrance Scholarships'. No real acronym or short form is in official use, so 'McGill Entrance Scholarships' is used as a clear short form rather than a documented acronym.

No legacy or alternative award names are recorded, because none were found on official mcgill.ca pages. The McGill Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong Entrance Scholarship and the One-Year Community Leadership Entrance Award are named sub-awards inside the same programme and are described in programme_structure.award_types rather than given separate titles.

Date convention. The SCHEMA_CONTRACT.v1 document states that 'today is 2026-10-03'. The actual verification date for this record is 2026-10-10, which is also the date used by the sibling Canada record 37-canada-ubc-international-scholars.json. last_verified_date, last_verified_at, _verification_timestamp and logo_verified_at are therefore recorded as 2026-10-10, and status and the cycle are assessed against that date.

Cycle. The record is written for the 2027 entry cycle, September 2027 intake. Applications for admission and for the Major Entrance Scholarship opened on October 1, 2026, so the cycle is open at the time of verification. The status field is OPEN because the application window is live, not because an award has been granted.

Deadline structure. McGill publishes one set of scholarship deadlines by applicant region rather than a single date for all applicants. The date recorded in application_deadline.deadline_date, 2027-01-21, is the deadline for applicants from schools outside of Canada, which is the relevant date for international applicants and the subject of this record. The regional alternatives, February 7 for the rest of Canada and March 7 for Quebec CEGEP, and the corresponding admission deadlines of January 15, February 1 and March 1, are recorded in typical_application_window and application_period rather than dropped. The timezone is taken verbatim from McGill's instruction that applications must be submitted 'no later than midnight, Montreal time (Eastern Standard Time)'.

Award amounts. Only figures published by McGill are recorded. One-year entrance scholarships are CAD $3,000 and non-renewable. Major Entrance Scholarships are published as a total range of CAD $12,000 to CAD $48,000 and as a per-annum range of CAD $3,000 to CAD $12,000, renewable for up to four years. The CAD $12,000-per-annum tier is explicitly restricted to Canadian citizens and legal permanent residents, so the CAD $48,000 figure is not presented as an achievable international award. No total award value is computed or asserted, and no per-award value is recorded for the donor-named awards that the official calendar publishes only as 'Award value: Varies'.

Tuition figures. No international tuition dollar rate is recorded. McGill publishes international undergraduate rates only inside PDF fee tables (new_intl_ugrad_degree_students_admitted_2026-27.pdf and bachelortuitionguaranteerates_communications.pdf) whose text could not be extracted from the binary PDF, so recording a figure would be fabrication. What is recorded is verified: the Quebec rate of CAD $103.92 per credit, the Canadian out-of-province Rate A of CAD $432.85 per credit (CAD $103.92 plus a CAD $328.93 supplement) for students admitted since Fall 2024, and the existence of the Guaranteed Tuition Model for international students in a bachelor's, DMD or MDCM degree, under which the international rate is set for the duration of the degree.

Need-blind status, stated precisely. No official mcgill.ca page read for this record uses the term 'need-blind' for international undergraduate admission, so this record does not assert it. The verified position is threefold: first, McGill states that entrance scholarships are entirely merit-based and that financial need is not considered; second, McGill states that admission is based on academic merit and space availability, with offers issued to the most competitive applicants first; third, need-based support is assessed separately through the Entrance Bursary Program and In-Course Financial Aid, where McGill states financial need is considered for all students including international students. Any future statement that McGill is need-blind for internationals should be sourced to an official mcgill.ca policy page before being added.

Contradiction recorded rather than resolved. The Entrance Bursary Program page states that 'financial need is considered for all McGill students, including international students' and that international students not eligible for government aid may still apply for an entrance bursary. The In-Course Financial Aid page separately states that 'first-year international students are generally not eligible for need-based aid from McGill' and that first-year international students must demonstrate financial capacity to obtain authorisation to study in Canada. Both statements are quoted with their URLs in source_citations. The reading adopted is that the Entrance Bursary Program is the first-year pathway for international applicants while the in-course programme is generally closed to them, but this is an interpretation and is flagged as such in risk_flags.

Need-based aid is a distinct programme, not part of this scholarship. The Entrance Bursary Program is described here because it is part of the international student funding structure an applicant must consider, and because McGill reports average offers of CAD $3,000 for Quebecers, CAD $9,000 for out-of-province Canadian students and CAD $19,000 for US and international students. Those figures are described by McGill as averages proportionate to the tuition rate based on residency, not as fixed award values, and are not recorded in funding or funding_breakdown, which cover the scholarship only.

English proficiency. Every score in english_requirement is traceable to the official English language proficiency page. IELTS 6.5 with components 6.0 and PTE Academic 65 with components 60 and CAEL 70 with components 60 are published as single figures for all undergraduate applicants. TOEFL and Duolingo are published by programme group, so the values recorded as minimum_toefl 90 and minimum_duolingo 125 are the figures for the general undergraduate group (Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Architecture, Arts, B.A. and Sc., Education, Engineering, Nursing, Physical and Occupational Therapy, Religious Studies, Science and Social Work); the higher programme-specific figures of TOEFL 100 or 5.0 and Duolingo 130 for Education TESL and Management, and the lower TOEFL 79-80 or 4.0 for Music, are stated explicitly in test_score_note so that no programme-specific rule is universalised. No TOEFL or other test validity period is published on the page read, so test_validity_months is null.

Academic minima are estimates, not thresholds. McGill labels the whole criteria table as estimated minima based on averages from historical data, states that the minima are for consideration only and may be lower or higher depending on available funds and applicant numbers, states that the table is for reference purposes only, and states that applicants are not guaranteed a scholarship even if they meet the standards listed. fixed_percentage_requirement is true only in the sense that McGill publishes numeric reference figures, and percentage_note carries the full qualification.

Renewal conditions are recorded in full because they materially affect value. A renewable award is not guaranteed for four years: it requires 27 McGill graded credits in the regular academic year, or 14 if registered for a single term, a probationary sessional GPA of 3.50 in the first year and 3.70 thereafter, and it excludes advanced-standing credits from AP, IB, French Baccalaureate and A-Levels. programme_duration year and month fields are left null because McGill expresses tenability in academic years and renewal conditions rather than a single duration figure; official_range and renewal_note carry the substance.

Extras and omissions. Two pieces of information have no natural home in the contract's fixed field list and are recorded as follows: the list of applicant categories explicitly excluded from entrance scholarships is stored inside the programme_structure open map as ineligible_applicants, and the single-award rule is recorded as top-level previous_award_restriction, which the contract expressly sanctions adding for a bachelor's award. b01-maeci-scholarships-foreign-students-italian-citizens-abroad.json is a separate record using a different six-key envelope schema and was not modified; 03-italy-maeci-ire-scholarships.json is an existing numbered-series record for a different scholarship and was not modified.

Logo. The logo_url is a real SVG asset served from the university's own domain, www.mcgill.ca/studentawards/themes/custom/miles/assets/svgs/logo.svg, referenced by the official McGill Student Awards site with the alt text 'McGill University logo'. It was fetched and confirmed to be a valid SVG McGill coat of arms on 2026-10-10. No third-party or aggregator source was used. image_url is null because no photograph was selected and verified; this is an honest null rather than a placeholder.

Untracked file. research/bachelor/ is untracked in this repository, so writing this file does not alter any tracked production data. The only tracked modification in the working tree, backend/config/programme_details.json, pre-dates this work and was not touched. No commit, push, merge or deployment was performed.

Completeness. _completeness_score is 0.93 rather than higher because several fields are honestly null for lack of an official published figure: the international tuition rate, every non-tuition funding component, the programme_duration year and month fields, test_validity_months, nationality_quota, total_estimated_value and official_universal_weighting, and because the need-blind question and one internal contradiction about international need-based aid remain unresolved from official sources.

Coverage items that are non-monetary are labelled as such in funding_breakdown.accommodation_support and in coverage, because McGill publishes a residence guarantee and priority registration rather than an accommodation grant. This prevents a housing benefit being read as a cash award.
